# Physics tools

Rigid bodies, characters, queries, settling and navigation meshes.

8 tools in the `physics` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`physics_add`](#physics_add) | Make entities physical with a preset (one undoable edit). |
| [`physics_query`](#physics_query) | Ask the collision world (colliders, not render meshes) — works while editing and playing. |
| [`physics_settle`](#physics_settle) | Drop objects with a real simulation and keep where they come to rest (simulate, then keep the poses). |
| [`physics_debug`](#physics_debug) | Capture the viewport with every collider drawn as a wireframe (color = state) plus physics stats (bodies, awake/asleep, contacts, triggers, characters, joints) and warnings (bad layers, unsupported shapes, missing joint targets). |
| [`physics_settings`](#physics_settings) | Read or change scene-wide physics: gravity (m/s^2), substeps (stability for stacks/fast objects), which collision layers ignore each other (ignorePairs, e.g. |
| [`nav_build`](#nav_build) | Bake (or rebuild) the navigation mesh from static colliders and static meshes, save it to the project and record the settings in the scene's `navmesh` component (one undoable edit; creates an entity named "Navigation" if needed). |
| [`nav_path`](#nav_path) | Walking path on the navmesh between two points or entities (bakes the navmesh first if needed). |
| [`nav_debug`](#nav_debug) | Top-down map of the level with the navmesh drawn over it (teal = walkable), nav agents (yellow dots) with their current paths, and optionally a test path between two points (orange). |

### `physics_add` { #physics_add }

**Make physical** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Make entities physical with a preset (one undoable edit). prop = dynamic rigid body with a collider fitted to its mesh and a mass estimated from its size; static_level = static colliders for every mesh under the entity (triangle-exact for imported models) — use on level roots; kinematic_platform = moved by its transform/scripts, carries and pushes things; player_character / npc_character = capsule character controller fitted to the mesh (drive with walk/jump in Wander); trigger_zone = sensor that fires `on trigger_enter`/`on trigger_exit`; debris = light, does not collide with characters; projectile = fast (continuous collision); remove = strip body/collider/character/joint. `overrides` patches the components, e.g. {"body": {"mass": 80, "restitution": 0.6}, "collider": {"shape": "sphere"}}. Example: {"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2"], "preset": "prop"}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Entity (or use entities) |  |
| `entities` | integer \| string[] |  | Entities to change |  |
| `preset` | string | yes | What the entities become | `prop` `static_level` `kinematic_platform` `player_character` `npc_character` `trigger_zone` `debris` `projectile` `remove` |
| `overrides` | object |  | Component patches, e.g. {"body": {...}, "collider": {...}, "character": {...}} |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    physics_add {"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2"], "preset": "prop"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call physics_add '{"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2"], "preset": "prop"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "physics_add",
        "arguments": {
          "entities": [
            "Crate 1",
            "Crate 2"
          ],
          "preset": "prop"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `physics_query` { #physics_query }

**Physics query** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Ask the collision world (colliders, not render meshes) — works while editing and playing. raycast = first hit along a ray; raycast_all = every entity along it; shapecast = sweep a sphere/box/capsule (will this fit / where does it land?); overlap = entities touching a shape at `origin` (is this spot free?). Triggers are ignored unless include_triggers. Example: {"type": "raycast", "origin": [0, 10, 0], "direction": [0, -1, 0]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | Query kind | `raycast` `raycast_all` `shapecast` `overlap` |
| `origin` | number[3] | yes | Ray/sweep start, or the overlap shape center |  |
| `direction` | number[3] |  | Ray/sweep direction (default [0,-1,0]) |  |
| `max_distance` | number |  | Max distance in m (default 100) |  |
| `shape` | string |  | shapecast/overlap shape (default sphere) | `sphere` `box` `capsule` |
| `radius` | number |  | Sphere/capsule radius (default 0.5) |  |
| `height` | number |  | Capsule total height (default 1.8) |  |
| `half_extents` | number[3] |  | Box half size (default [0.5,0.5,0.5]) |  |
| `rotation` | number[3] |  | Shape rotation, Euler degrees |  |
| `exclude` | integer \| string[] |  | Entities to ignore |  |
| `include_triggers` | boolean |  | Also report trigger zones |  |
| `layers` | string[] |  | Only these collision layers |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    physics_query {"type": "raycast", "origin": [0, 10, 0], "direction": [0, -1, 0]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call physics_query '{"type": "raycast", "origin": [0, 10, 0], "direction": [0, -1, 0]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "physics_query",
        "arguments": {
          "type": "raycast",
          "origin": [
            0,
            10,
            0
          ],
          "direction": [
            0,
            -1,
            0
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `physics_settle` { #physics_settle }

**Settle with physics** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Drop objects with a real simulation and keep where they come to rest (simulate, then keep the poses). Only the listed entities move (as dynamic bodies, even without a body component); everything else is frozen. The result is ONE undoable edit. Great after scatter/place: rocks, crates, books and debris end up naturally stacked and resting instead of floating or intersecting. Example: {"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2", "Barrel"], "seconds": 4}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | integer \| string |  | Entity to settle (or use entities) |  |
| `entities` | integer \| string[] |  | Entities to settle (top-level props) |  |
| `seconds` | number |  | Max simulated seconds (default 4, max 30); stops early when everything sleeps |  |
| `freeze_others` | boolean |  | Keep other dynamic bodies still (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    physics_settle {"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2", "Barrel"], "seconds": 4}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call physics_settle '{"entities": ["Crate 1", "Crate 2", "Barrel"], "seconds": 4}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "physics_settle",
        "arguments": {
          "entities": [
            "Crate 1",
            "Crate 2",
            "Barrel"
          ],
          "seconds": 4
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `physics_debug` { #physics_debug }

**See colliders** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Capture the viewport with every collider drawn as a wireframe (color = state) plus physics stats (bodies, awake/asleep, contacts, triggers, characters, joints) and warnings (bad layers, unsupported shapes, missing joint targets). Use it to check that colliders match the visuals, triggers sit where you expect, and props fall asleep. view: editor (default), scene camera, or top (orthographic map).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | string |  | Camera | `editor` `scene` `top` |
| `focus` | integer \| string |  | Frame this entity |  |
| `width` | integer |  | Image width (default 768) |  |
| `height` | integer |  | Image height (default 432) |  |
| `show_static` | boolean |  | Draw static colliders (default true) |  |
| `include_image` | boolean |  | Return the image (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    physics_debug {"view": "top"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call physics_debug '{"view": "top"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "physics_debug",
        "arguments": {
          "view": "top"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `physics_settings` { #physics_settings }

**Physics settings** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Read or change scene-wide physics: gravity (m/s^2), substeps (stability for stacks/fast objects), which collision layers ignore each other (ignorePairs, e.g. "debris-player, projectile-projectile"), sleeping, on/off. Stored in a `physics_world` component (created on an entity named "Physics" when you first change it). Example: {"gravity": [0, -1.62, 0]} for the Moon.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gravity` | number[3] |  | Gravity vector in m/s^2 |  |
| `substeps` | integer |  | Collision steps per tick (1..8) |  |
| `ignorePairs` | string |  | Layer pairs that never collide, comma separated |  |
| `allowSleep` | boolean |  | Let resting bodies sleep |  |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | Simulate physics while playing |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    physics_settings {"gravity": [0, -1.62, 0]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call physics_settings '{"gravity": [0, -1.62, 0]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "physics_settings",
        "arguments": {
          "gravity": [
            0,
            -1.62,
            0
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `nav_build` { #nav_build }

**Bake navmesh** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Bake (or rebuild) the navigation mesh from static colliders and static meshes, save it to the project and record the settings in the scene's `navmesh` component (one undoable edit; creates an entity named "Navigation" if needed). Re-run after changing the level layout. Settings default to the navmesh component's: agent_radius (walls eroded by it), agent_height, max_climb (steps), max_slope (degrees), cell_size (precision). Entities tagged "nav_ignore" are left out. Then use nav_path / nav_debug, or nav agents and navigate() in Wander.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_radius` | number |  | Agent radius in m (default 0.4) |  |
| `agent_height` | number |  | Agent height in m (default 1.8) |  |
| `max_climb` | number |  | Highest step in m (default 0.4) |  |
| `max_slope` | number |  | Steepest walkable slope in degrees (default 45) |  |
| `cell_size` | number |  | Voxel size in m (default 0.2; smaller = more precise, slower) |  |
| `cell_height` | number |  | Voxel height in m (default 0.1) |  |
| `tile_size` | integer |  | Cells per tile (default 64) |  |
| `geometry` | string |  | Input geometry (default both) | `both` `colliders` `meshes` |
| `save` | boolean |  | Write the navmesh file (default true) |  |
| `path` | string |  | Project-relative file (default: next to the scene, &lt;scene&gt;.navmesh) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    nav_build {"agent_radius": 0.4, "agent_height": 1.8, "max_climb": 0.4, "max_slope": 45, "cell_size": 0.2}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call nav_build '{"agent_radius": 0.4, "agent_height": 1.8, "max_climb": 0.4, "max_slope": 45, "cell_size": 0.2}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "nav_build",
        "arguments": {
          "agent_radius": 0.4,
          "agent_height": 1.8,
          "max_climb": 0.4,
          "max_slope": 45,
          "cell_size": 0.2
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `nav_path` { #nav_path }

**Find path** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Walking path on the navmesh between two points or entities (bakes the navmesh first if needed). Returns the corner points, the walking length, and whether the goal is reachable (partial = it is not; the path ends at the closest reachable point). Use to check that a level is traversable or to plan patrols. Example: {"from": "Player", "to": [12, 0, -4]}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | any | yes | Start: [x, y, z] or an entity |  |
| `to` | any | yes | Goal: [x, y, z] or an entity |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    nav_path {"from": "Player", "to": [12, 0, -4]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call nav_path '{"from": "Player", "to": [12, 0, -4]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "nav_path",
        "arguments": {
          "from": "Player",
          "to": [
            12,
            0,
            -4
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `nav_debug` { #nav_debug }

**See navmesh** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Top-down map of the level with the navmesh drawn over it (teal = walkable), nav agents (yellow dots) with their current paths, and optionally a test path between two points (orange). The fastest way to spot unreachable rooms, doorways too narrow for agents, and gaps. Bakes the navmesh first if needed.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `focus` | integer \| string |  | Frame this entity instead of the whole navmesh |  |
| `from` | any |  | Optional test path start: [x, y, z] or an entity |  |
| `to` | any |  | Optional test path goal |  |
| `size` | integer |  | Image size in pixels (default 640) |  |
| `include_image` | boolean |  | Return the image (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    nav_debug {"from": "Player", "to": [12, 0, -4], "size": 800}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call nav_debug '{"from": "Player", "to": [12, 0, -4], "size": 800}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "nav_debug",
        "arguments": {
          "from": "Player",
          "to": [
            12,
            0,
            -4
          ],
          "size": 800
        }
      }
    }
    ```
